resources.string: Settings are protected with a PIN.
Two special permissions are needed to measure app time and to show the block screen. Grant them, then come back here.
Required. Lets Screenkeeper see which app is open and for how long.
Required. Lets the block screen appear on top of an app.
Optional. Warns you 5 minutes before a limit.
Recommended on phones, so limits keep working in the background.

Toggle greyed out, \"Controlled by restricted setting\"? Android locks this for apps installed from a browser or file manager. Open App info, tap the ⋮ menu in the top corner → Allow restricted settings, then come back here.
Settings screen missing? Show ADB commands
Some TVs hide these settings. Enable Developer options and network debugging on the device, then run these from a computer (after adb connect <device-ip>):
Select an app to set limits. Long-press to open it.
Remove all rules for this app
It can\'t be opened right now.
This app is allowed between %1$s and %2$s.
The daily limit of %1$s is used up. It resets at midnight.
Stretch, grab some water, rest your eyes. Back in:
Enter the PIN to open this app.
Enter the PIN to open this app. The PIN schedule asks for it until %1$s.
Enter the PIN to open this app. This app\'s own setting asks for the PIN at all times (its Rules → Require PIN to open), whatever the PIN schedule says.
Enter the PIN to open this app. This app\'s own PIN times ask for it until %1$s.
Control a TV from this device
Turn this on to set limits and PINs on this TV from the Screenkeeper app on your phone. The TV and the phone must be on the same Wi-Fi.
Set limits on your NVIDIA Shield or other Android TV from here. Install Screenkeeper on the TV and turn on \"Allow control from a phone\" there.
On your phone, open Screenkeeper → Control a TV and enter this code. Address if the TV isn\'t found automatically: %1$s
The TV needs Screenkeeper installed with \"Allow control from a phone\" turned on. Both devices must be on the same network.
Searching for TVs on your network…
Shown on the TV under Phone remote (also in the TV\'s network settings).
Nothing answered at %1$s. Check that the TV is on, Screenkeeper is open or running, and \"Allow control from a phone\" is on.
Enter the 6-digit code shown on the TV under Phone remote.
The code didn\'t match. Read it from the TV screen and try again. After 5 wrong tries the TV waits a minute.
The TV no longer knows this phone. Pair again.
Is the TV on and on the same Wi-Fi? Screenkeeper must be running on it with \"Allow control from a phone\" turned on.
Select an app to set its limits on %1$s.
%1$s can be used for 15 more minutes, whatever the rules say.
Lets a phone paired under Phone remote type into text fields on this TV. It only acts when a paired phone sends text, and only touches the focused text field.
Type on this TV from your phone. Turn on \"Screenkeeper phone keyboard\" in the accessibility settings that open (on a Shield: Settings → Device Preferences → Accessibility).
Can\'t find it? Show ADB commands
From a computer, after adb connect <tv-ip>. Note: this replaces any other accessibility services that are turned on.
Select a search box or text field on the TV, then type here. Text appears on the TV as you type.
Password field — text isn\'t shown back
No text field on the TV right now. Open a search box or login screen there.
The keyboard isn\'t turned on on the TV. On the TV: Screenkeeper → Phone remote → Phone keyboard.
This app on the TV didn\'t accept the text. Some apps use their own on-screen keyboard that can\'t be typed into from outside.
The keyboard isn\'t running on the TV (an app update can switch it off). Press Fix to turn it back on from this phone — it uses the TV\'s Network debugging, like Update TV over ADB.
Couldn\'t fix it: %1$s\n\nCheck that Network debugging is on (TV: Settings → Device Preferences → Developer options), or on the TV open Screenkeeper → Phone keyboard.
Android ticked the keyboard but didn\'t start it, which can happen after an update. Press the button above, or use Fix from this phone in the phone\'s keyboard screen.
Screenkeeper on the TV is too old for the keyboard. Update it there.
Install Screenkeeper (or any APK) on the TV straight from this phone — no computer. Your rules and PIN on the TV are kept.
Install this phone\'s Screenkeeper %1$s on the TV
Look at the TV: tick \"Always allow from this computer\" and choose OK. (Only the first time.)
Installed. Screenkeeper on the TV restarts by itself.
Granting usage access, overlay, battery and keyboard…
Done: usage access, display over other apps, battery exemption and the phone keyboard are on.
Enter the TV\'s IP address, e.g. 192.168.1.50 or 192.168.1.50:5555.

The TV\'s copy was signed with a different key, so it can\'t be updated in place. Uninstall Screenkeeper on the TV once (this clears its rules), then install again. A fixed signing key in CI avoids this — see the README.
The TV already has a newer version than this APK.

On the TV, once: Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on Build 7 times. Then Settings → Device Preferences → Developer options → Network debugging: On. The IP shown there is the address above (port 5555).
Estimated from Android\'s monthly totals, from before Screenkeeper kept its own history. No daily details.
No usage recorded for this period. Screenkeeper keeps history from the day it was updated to this version (plus about a week before).
When the screen is used, by hour
Screenkeeper on the TV is too old for statistics. Update it there (Update TV over ADB).
Some months are estimates from Android\'s monthly totals.
Ask for the PIN during certain hours — for all apps, or only the ones you tick. Each app can also have its own PIN times under its rules.
Every app except Screenkeeper and the home screen
Off. When on, the PIN is needed between %1$s.

resources.string: An app asks for the PIN when its own setting or the schedule says so — so these keep asking outside the schedule\'s hours.
Let the schedule decide for these apps
Times after midnight count for the day before: with Friday ticked, the PIN is still needed on Saturday until %1$s.
No days are ticked, so the schedule never asks for the PIN.
